name: North Polar Layered Deposits
blurb: The edge of the north polar ice cap at 85 N: a kilometre-high scarp of layered water ice and dust above a dark embayment, the cap's surface cut by fractures and frosted with seasonal CO2.

projection.name: Equirectangular, Mars 2000 sphere, true scale at 85.108 deg (latTs = lat0), centred on 237.47 E
projection.note: x = R cos(lat_ts) (lon - lon_0), y = R lat (radians): projected metres are true metres at the site's latitude; cos_lat0 (the world scale factor) is therefore 1

grid.convention: sample (i,j) of a level is centred at x0+(i+0.5)*mpp, y0-(j+0.5)*mpp; tile (tx,ty) holds samples tx*tile.. and ty*tile..
grid.world: game X = east metres from the site centre = x - x_centre; game Z = south metres = y_centre - y; game Y = height_m - height.ref

height.encoding: height_m = offset + (R*256 + G) * scale; B = provenance

provenance_byte.64: MGS MOLA north polar gridded topography, 512 pixels per degree (115 m), MEGDR megt_n_512_1 (115 m posts)
provenance_byte.0: no data (filled from the nearest valid sample)

64.text: MGS MOLA north polar gridded topography, 512 pixels per degree (115 m), MEGDR megt_n_512_1

labels.0: no data (filled from the nearest valid sample)

levelling.method: each layer stretched to 8 bits once per site (0.5 / 99.5 percentiles of the first layer; later layers matched to it in mean and spread where they overlap), then feathered in priority order

imagery.colour: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour (232 m), resampled to 80 m: modulates the hue of the ground; the brightness comes from the imagery

colour_tex.what: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour (232 m), resampled to 80 m: modulates the hue of the ground; the brightness comes from the imagery

levels.what: MGS MOLA north polar gridded topography, 512 pixels per degree (115 m), cubic-resampled to 16 m
the 16 m level upsampled to 4 m with a cubic B-spline: interpolation, nothing finer than the source posts
Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic, 232 m (232 m), resampled to 20 m
levels.label: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic, 232 m, 232 m

mola_np.title: MGS MOLA north polar gridded topography, 512 pixels per degree (115 m), MEGDR megt_n_512_1
mola_np.composition: Median MOLA altimetry per 115 m bin, polar stereographic, heights above the areoid (raw * 0.25 - 8000 m); bins with no shot interpolated by the MOLA team
mola_np.georeferencing: the label gives no projection offsets; the grid was registered as polar stereographic centred on the pole, lon 0 toward the bottom (checked against the MOLA-HRSC blend at six points: within 0 to 92 m, median 2 m)
mola_np.licence: Public domain (NASA / GSFC MOLA Science Team). Cite Smith et al. 2001, JGR 106(E10), and Neumann et al. 2003.
mola_np.bytes_measured_by: size of the whole file, downloaded once

colour.title: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic, 232 m (USGS Astrogeology)
colour.composition: Viking Orbiter images (MDIM 2.1) coloured from Viking colour observations; used here only as a low-resolution colour tint
colour.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. Cite USGS Astrogeology, Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized mosaic (NASA / JPL / USGS).

tint.from: hue of the darkest, middle and brightest fifths of the Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic over the site (dark and bright pulled halfway to the middle; a hue that is not red > green > blue falls back to the game's own); brightness kept from the game's default ramp

pois.name: Landing
pois.note: The top of the cap, about 3.2 km below the datum: water ice under a seasonal skin of CO2 frost, flat enough for the descent engines.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Polar outpost site
pois.note: A level stretch of the cap a kilometre back from the scarp edge: room for the outpost, and the embayment's dark floor a kilometre below to the south.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Ice core site
pois.note: Where the drill goes down through the layered deposits: each layer a few metres of ice and dust, a climate record from Mars' changing tilt (Laskar et al. 2002 put the upper layers at a few million years).
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Crevasse field
pois.note: Near the scarp edge the ice is fractured into a network of narrow cracks. The fractures here are generated: MOLA's 115 m grid cannot resolve them, though HiRISE shows real ones along polar scarps.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

notes: North of 80 degrees the site's equirectangular grid (true scale at 85.11 N) stretches east-west distances by up to 3.5% at its northern and southern edges.
The only imagery mosaicked this far north is Viking's (232 m); the scarp's layers, the ice, the fractures and the frost on screen are generated from the terrain, not photographed.

MOLA polar grid registered by hand (the label gives no projection offsets): polar stereographic on the 3376.2 km sphere, centred on the pole, lon 0 toward the bottom; checked against the MOLA-HRSC blend at six points (median 2 m).
quality: MOLA polar topography 115 m; Viking MDIM 2.1 imagery 232 m (no finer imagery is mosaicked here)
